correctness.rationale: Exact symbolic first-occurrence counting gives the escape root, whose unique physical branch lies within \(2q^{-n}\) of one for \(n\ge3\). A word-uniform \(O_q(nq^{-n})\) normalized-rate estimate, primitive-block counting, and a \(O_q(q^{-R})\) tail for squared deviations allow interchange of the depth and finite-period limits. Mean centering costs \(O_q(n^2q^{-n})\). The accompanied standalone checker verifies finite consequences, rather than replacing the proof.

originality.rationale: The closest 2012 Markov-hole paper proves single-hole formulas and the ensemble first moment but not the asymptotic second centered moment or its variance-weighted primitive-period law; accessible primary comparisons, exact-formula and alias searches, and published mathematical-result comparisons uncovered no covering theorem. The source formulas are explicitly credited and bibliographic priority remains a nonzero risk. Bonanno–Cristadoro–Lenci arXiv:2112.14248, a close exact-model source, was inspected through its main theorems and generating-function appendix and found to classify maximizers, not ensemble second moments.
residual_risks: The spectral/primitive-orbit apparatus of arXiv:1207.7000 makes the new variance derivable; an earlier unindexed or differently framed second-moment calculation may exist.
No independent expert historical or mathematical audit has been performed.
Arbitrary intervals, nonuniform invariant densities, time-random holes and growing-q joint limits are outside the proved scope.

The later Bonanno–Cristadoro–Lenci paper treats exactly the same full-shift hole object, so historical priority risk includes its broader references and possible unstated derived moment facts; its examined results do not contain the quantitative moment theorem.

value.rationale: For the natural uniform-position ensemble of equal-measure fixed leaks, the exact \(q^{-n}\) variance scale and infinite primitive-orbit constant quantify heterogeneity invisible to mean escape-rate asymptotics. The limiting weighted period law explains the entire allocation to rare short-cycle holes and is a meaningful nontrivial dynamical invariant across every fixed integer slope.
